incidents.victim: Latin American government agencies (Guatemala, Honduras, Panama, Venezuela, Peru, Argentina, Puerto Rico)
incidents.vector: Custom 'SparroWocky' backdoor deployed to government networks; malware evades analysis, exfiltrates files and screenshots, and draws from open-source code to hinder attribution.
incidents.impact: Long-running campaign active since August 2025 provides persistent access to seven Latin American governments, including Panamanian agencies tied to canal port disputes at the center of US-China tensions; files, credentials, and system data exfiltrated.

incidents.vector: Unknown initial access; hackers (group calling itself CikLeak) exfiltrated internal documents, server configurations, passwords, and developer communications from Russia's election infrastructure and contractor networks.
incidents.impact: Internal documents, developer chats, and credentials reportedly stolen from Russia's Central Election Commission and Rostelecom days before the State Duma elections; Russia's CEC chair confirmed a surge in pre-election attacks; election infrastructure integrity questioned.

incidents.vector: Storm-2945 (a subcluster of Russia's Midnight Blizzard) manipulates DNS and HTTP traffic on hospitality networks to redirect travelers into device-code phishing via legitimate Microsoft sign-in pages, or to fake software updates that deliver credential-harvesting malware.
incidents.impact: Credentials, session tokens, security configurations, and remote-access history collected from victims; a single network interaction can result in either cloud identity compromise or full endpoint compromise; campaign dubbed 'CaptiveCrunch' by Microsoft.

incidents.victim: US sanctions regime / IRGC financial networks
incidents.vector: OFAC-designated financier Babak Zanjani operated BitBank, an Iranian cryptocurrency exchange, to transfer hundreds of millions in Bitcoin to the IRGC, evading US sanctions through a network of digital asset infrastructure and shell entities.
incidents.impact: US Treasury OFAC sanctioned BitBank and five associated individuals under Operation Economic Outcast; the exchange transferred hundreds of millions in Bitcoin to the IRGC between June and July 2026; also used by IRGC-linked Hormuz Safe Marine Services Authority.

incidents.vector: The Gentlemen ransomware group (RaaS) exploits publicly exposed VPN and web services, enumerates Active Directory using BloodHound, and deploys ESXi-targeting ransomware; Qilin uses AI-generated destructive scripts to accelerate attacks.
incidents.impact: 90 Japanese organizations hit in H1 2026, a 4.7% YoY increase; 80% are small/medium enterprises; The Gentlemen's global leak-site listings more than doubled (48 to 105 per month); double-extortion with data theft; Russian-speaking individuals suspected in The Gentlemen operations.

incidents.victim: Cisco Identity Services Engine users (enterprise network infrastructure)
incidents.vector: Authentication bypass in Cisco Identity Services Engine API (CVE-2026-76460, CVSS 10.0) allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to gain full device control over the system that enforces network access policy for the entire enterprise.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation confirmed before patch; attackers can modify network access policies, extract stored credentials, delete logs, and move laterally into every network segment ISE controls; CISA added to KEV catalog; no workarounds available.

incidents.victim: South Korean media and automotive companies
incidents.vector: HAProxy open-source load balancers compromised and implanted with a custom Linux toolkit (TED) that intercepts already-decrypted plaintext traffic; attackers write directly to raw TCP sockets and scrub log file counters to eliminate all forensic traces.
incidents.impact: Long-term espionage operations ongoing since early 2025 with zero anomalous processes or log entries; credential harvesting and watering-hole attacks give access to journalist source networks, unpublished reporting, and automotive manufacturing IP; TED represents an evolution of DPRK tradecraft into production infrastructure.

incidents.vector: SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-76461) in Cisco Secure Email Gateway allows arbitrary remote code execution by sending a specially crafted email; the process runs as root.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation confirmed; any organization using Cisco's email gateway may be fully compromised via a single malicious inbound email with no authentication required; Cisco published indicators of compromise; second Cisco actively-exploited zero-day in two days.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized third party accessed Revolut's systems and exfiltrated sensitive customer records; breach method not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Sensitive records of hundreds of customers exposed; attackers publicly posted a $3 million ransom demand threatening to sell data to other criminal groups within 24 hours; Revolut stated no direct contact has been received from any group claiming responsibility.

incidents.victim: Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source users (global e-commerce)
incidents.vector: Critical unauthenticated remote code execution via template engine injection (CVE-2026-75650) in the /graphql endpoint of Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source; no authentication required.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation confirmed by Australia's ACSC with substantial vulnerable instances in the Australian economy; allows complete server compromise of online storefronts; patch released September 7, 2026; organizations using unpatched versions remain at high risk.

incidents.victim: Software developers and enterprises using AI coding tools
incidents.vector: UNC6780 (TeamPCP) published trojanized MCP server packages to PyPI/npm and injected malicious code into official GitHub repositories; DUSTMAKER credential stealer targets AI coding assistants via prompt injection, hidden directory persistence, and CI/CD pipeline hijacking with LLM security scanner evasion.
incidents.impact: Large-scale supply chain compromises across PyPI, npm, and Docker Hub since March 2026; one enterprise victim had its proprietary AI repository exfiltrated and ransomed under LAPSUS branding; DUSTMAKER bypasses LLM security tools using embedded adversarial prompts; stolen credentials sold or used in ransomware partnerships.

incidents.vector: Dark web service selling digital scans of driver's licenses apparently sourced from a breach of a widely-used Louisiana-based identity verification company; images sold individually and in bulk.
incidents.impact: Over 153 million US and Canadian driver's license scans available for purchase, including records for high-ranking government officials such as US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth; FBI New Orleans field office opened formal investigation; poses significant identity theft and national security risk.

incidents.victim: International commercial tankers (Gulf of Mexico / Strait of Gibraltar)
incidents.vector: Foreign cyber actors compromised operational and IT networks of US-bound oil tankers; one vessel (VL Prosperity) had its engine speed remotely increased and fuel/engine-oil tank systems disabled while transiting the Strait of Gibraltar.
incidents.impact: VL Prosperity lost all communications for 30 hours; FBI and Coast Guard conducted joint cybersecurity boardings of two tankers in the Gulf of Mexico on August 21 and 24; US government is now tracking cyber threats against approximately 20 ships worldwide; attacks linked by analysts to the ongoing US-Iran conflict.
